name: Kuta: precolonial fortifications
description: Barangays of the sixteenth century defended themselves with kuta or kota: enclosures of sharpened timber or bamboo stakes, sometimes with earthworks, ditches and lookout platforms, where people could gather when raiders came by sea. Spanish accounts of the islands mention such stockades, and the word survives in place names. In this game the Kuta is drawn as a small palisade with a gate and a raised, thatched lookout reached by a ladder. The design is generic, the same for every tradition, and waits for a historian's review.
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
